propositions: A test assertion can pass when the contract it guards is violated because the oracle is weak or incomplete, but discovery.md concerns #1-11 do not ask whether assertions can fail on contract violations.

Two production bugs (0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e and 9bb7-4430-1202-4d93) escaped because oracle-strength antipatterns already catalogued in code-review-tests.md were not applied to the resting tree, only to diffs.

The rubric of oracle antipatterns exists but is not reachable: concern #12 must add it to discovery.md sharded by test region like concern #11, cite the rubric, and provide a portable fallback in references/patterns.md for repos without the rubric.

The schema at discovery.md:152 hardcodes 'eleven concerns' while the concern list is about to gain #12, creating a silent disagreement that nothing fails; an executable test deriving both counts must enforce consistency.

A test-only finding currently takes prod_impact=none from file path rather than from the guarded production contract, allowing weak-oracle findings below the impact floor; verification.md must re-anchor on the contract and require tree-state proof of harm reachability.
